title: Convergent Rollback Orchestration Slate
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Design an interactive rollback orchestration UI for the Redwood Console that helps engineers make fast, confident rollback decisions during canary and A/B rollouts. The slate centers on a "rollback playlist": a guided, ordered set of mitigation steps (traffic shift, model variant swap, throttled fallback, emergency snapshot revert) with signal anchors, simulated outcomes, and one-click execution. The flow must surface cost delta, SLO impact, and required approvals, and integrate with existing rollout timelines and telemetry dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive playlist UI shows ordered mitigation steps and allows reordering, skip, and preview
Signal anchors (latency, error rate, quality regression) are configurable per step and visually annotated in timeline and charts
Simulator runs a lightweight traffic preview producing expected user exposure and cost delta estimates within the console without requiring infra changes
One-click execution buttons produce an actionable runbook (links to PR, incident channel, on-call paging) and emit rollout events to traces/logs
Design includes accessible confirmations, reversible quick-revert, and inline audit summary for compliance
Design handoff assets (Figma, interaction spec, and acceptance handoff) uploaded and reviewed by Eng and PM
design_notes: Decision: Favor a deterministic 'playlist' representation over freeform textual runbooks to reduce operator ambiguity during incidents

Trade-off: Simulator will use heuristics (traffic model + historical signal multipliers) rather than exact infra simulation to keep UX responsive. We accept approximate cost/SLO deltas with confidence intervals
Constraint: Must reuse existing rollout timeline components; avoid adding new global state in Console to keep migration incremental
Accessibility: Color pairs and shapes used to indicate severity to meet AA contrast and avoid sole color reliance
Privacy/compliance: Audit summary must surface who executed steps and a snapshot id; design includes optional KMS key reference field for Private deployments
